newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen volatility dips after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen volatility dips after jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen edged lower in U.S. options trading following the release of the April jobs report and with the weekend looming.

One-month dollar/yen was 8.25/8.50 percent, down slightly from pre-report levels of 8.30/8.60 percent and around 8.50/8.70 percent the previous session. One-year dollar/yen was roughly unchanged at 9.25/9.40 percent.
Selling short-dated volatility was the post-report focus, but analysts said activity was pretty subdued and indicative of the overall view of the dollar's direction.
"Sentiment is the dollar drifts higher, but not at an alarming pace," said Ted Voorhees, senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York.
Now, with the widely watched employment report out of the way and a budget agreement almost sewn up, money managers apparently have assessed there is less need to hedge risk, options analysts said.
"Everything has been removed from the table," Voorhees said.
April U.S. employment numbers were mixed for financial markets, with nonfarm payrolls rising a mild 142,000 but the unemployment rate falling to just 4.9 percent, a 24-year low.
Six-month dollar/yen options were actively traded late Thursday, with $900 million at-the-money yen puts and another $200 million in 20-delta 130.00 yen puts said to have changed hands.
The dollar at midday was bid at 126.58 yen.

Dollar/mark was even more unfazed by the jobs report, options traders said. One-month volatility hovered around 8.40/8.70 percent all morning, and one-year was trading at 9.00/9.30 percent. Values were virtually the same Thursday.

Dollar/mark bullishness has cooled, with long-term trend resistance at 1.74 marks looking increasingly formidable, said an options analyst for a West Coast bank. The dollar was just below 1.73 marks at midday.
Risk reversals, the put-call pricing differential, shifted to neutral from their former mark put skew, suggesting more poeple are questioning whether the dollar has topped, the analyst said.
In dollar/yen, the one-month 25-delta risk reversal was 0.1 bid for yen calls.

Cable volatilities were easing back down in U.S. trading from a morning peak in Britain following Labour's election sweep. For a brief moment, "there was a lot of panic for something that was widely anticipated," Voorhees said.
